written: 2026-10-26, before any full-grid DEDi pair was run on a run of the analysis order (only the timing pilot on index 38, which is outside the hard-120 analysis set, had run)
question: Does DEDi with its authors' full hyperparameter grid close the gap to our final model on hard-120, where reduced-grid DEDi (lambda in {1e-2,1}, R in {1e-4,1e-2}) lost 26/5?
ours: final model results already stored in results_hard120/ours_hard120.json; not rerun
grid: the paper grid from the authors' example notebooks ('Parameters used in paper'): lambda = 10^{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3}, R = 10^{-4,-3,-2,-1,0}; 35 pairs. Contains the 4 reduced-grid pairs.
method: benchmarks/dedi_fullgrid.py: authors' code unmodified (same shim as before), same 20-term degree-3 library, same every-third-sample validation mask, FindBestModel defaults (LM, max_iterations 500, tolerance 1e-5). Each (run, lambda, R) pair is a separate FindBestModel([lambda],[R]) call; equivalent to the joint call because the authors' loop resets all optimisation state between pairs.
selection_rule_primary: per run, the pair with the lowest validation error (FindBestModel's default output_sort='Validation'); NaN as +inf; ties to the first pair in the authors' loop order (lambda outer, R inner). If any of the run's 35 pairs raises, the run counts as a DEDi failure (as the original runner would).
selection_secondary: (1) validation BIC (the other criterion DEDi computes); (2) oracle: exact if any of the 35 pairs is exact (uses the truth; an upper bound on what any selection rule over this grid could achieve, not a method); (3) errored pairs dropped instead of failing the run, reported only if it changes anything.
subset: results_dedi_fullgrid/order.json, made by `python benchmarks/dedi_fullgrid_report.py --make-order` (numpy default_rng seed 20261026) from the 114-run hard-120 analysis set. Strata by (final exact, reduced DEDi exact): A = final only (26), B = reduced DEDi only (5), D = neither (3), C = both (80). Order: random permutation of A+B+D (the 34 runs where full-grid DEDi could change the head-to-head in DEDi's favour or lose a DEDi win) in blocks of 3, each block followed by one run from a random permutation of C (where the full grid can only cost DEDi). Not a selection on full-grid outcomes.
analysis_set: the longest prefix of order.json in which all 35 pairs of every run finished by the deadline. Runs finished outside the prefix are not analysed.
compute: DGX Spark, 10 single-core workers pinned to cores 10-19 (taskset), thread env vars 1, run-major task order so runs complete roughly in order. Hard deadline 2026-10-27 13:00 EDT (workers killed then). Main job starts on each core as soon as the pilot worker on that core finishes (~16:00 on 2026-10-26). Cost estimate from the first 10 pilot pairs: 11-22 min per pair on one core, i.e. roughly 9-13 core-hours per run, so about 18-22 runs are expected in the analysis set (about 14-16 from A+B+D and 5 from C). Resumable after a crash (same order, finished pairs skipped).
metrics: exact support recovery; false positives/negatives; chosen (lambda, R); median relative coefficient error where both exact; cost per pair and per run
tests: on the analysis set, overall, per system and per stratum: final vs full-grid DEDi paired W/L with two-sided exact sign test (primary); final vs reduced-grid DEDi on the same runs; full vs reduced DEDi (exact McNemar = sign test on discordant runs). Secondary: stratum-weighted projection of final vs full-grid W/L to all 114 runs (point estimate; sampled strata only).
decision: Reported as is, either way. If full-grid DEDi is not significantly worse than the final model on the analysis set, the hard-120 claim is restated as 'better than reduced-grid DEDi' only.
pilot: index 38 (Lorenz, outside the 114-run analysis set), all 35 pairs, run first to estimate cost and to check that the 4 reduced-grid pairs reproduce the stored reduced-grid choice; reported separately.
